children: In interim data as of September 8, 2026, 8 of 9 evaluable patients had a clinically meaningful SLEDAI-2K reduction; 4 of 7 patients with elevated baseline proteinuria achieved complete renal responses within 24 weeks. The ongoing study had treated 12 patients.
Renal responses are a potentially important efficacy signal, but come from a small evaluable group in an ongoing early-phase study.
Broad disease-activity improvement adds evidence of clinical activity, though the sample is small and follow-up is interim.
The limited treated population constrains confidence in both efficacy and safety conclusions.
No dose-limiting toxicities or Grade ≥3 CRS
Early tolerability may support continued development; safety findings may change with more patients and follow-up.

This is an early clinical signal for Cullinan's licensed BCMA-directed candidate, based on interim data from a small Phase 1b/2a study. Further patient follow-up and additional clinical data will be needed to confirm efficacy and safety and support the global development plan.
